outcomes: A run that may publish knows its bound commit's ancestry and holds its publish credential before any repository code runs
A bound request without invocation.publication only gates: it plans no publication and starts no publication provider

A run whose credential provider negotiates publication-v1 and uploader-v1 resolves, opens, uploads and releases through that one session, and neither the engine nor a repository process asks for or holds a publish credential
nonGoals: Uploading under publication-v1 a member of an ecosystem other than npm, Go modules, OCI images and the Put registry, or a Put registry member of a kind put-write/v1 does not publish; such a plan is refused before it opens
Running a migration's data acceptance or moving a site-content channel at upload; the provider's release does both

requirements.text: A run naming a registry publisher or a release-set consumer, or a bound request with invocation.publication, reads the ancestry of its bound commit (PUTNAMI_SOURCE_REVISION, else HEAD) at process start, before the bootstrap, an install or a hook, ignoring replace refs, grafts and the commit-graph; the run reuses it. It names a shallow clone and holds an error above 1,000,000 commits. Other runs read none. With publish enabled, the credential provider starts before the first hook, locally as on a hosted run.

A bound request without invocation.publication enables no publish purpose, even when its invocation.providers names publish, and says so on stderr. When its plan holds a task of a publication command or with declared registry or cloud effects, or its versions start a release-set publication, the executing engine refuses it before any release-set or deploy provider starts. A gate-only request plans no publish job and starts no release-set provider.

The engine uses publication-v1 only when the provider echoes it; otherwise nothing changes. With it, the provider resolves channels, one open sends plan, heads and ancestry after the barrier, and release sends artifacts, heads, ancestry and evidence. The provider refuses a second plan and a non-ancestor head. Open and release retry once after a timeout on a live session; release is idempotent by plan digest. A refusal names its code and moves no channel. Local and hosted runs open one plan.

Under publication-v1 a publication job gets a private 0700 outbox and no credential. An upload node refuses a member the plan does not assign and sends it once, within a size bound, to the provider session that echoed uploader-v1, which re-hashes it and uploads with its own credential. The engine asks no credential, checks the answered digest and links no registry client. A reused job, or a put member with no upload, fails the release. A hosted session without uploader-v1 fails before the first hook.

A bound request with invocation.publication publishes through publication-v1 when the credential provider echoes it, as a local run does: open waits for its barrier commands, and the provider receives the plan digest a local run of the commit opens. Its expected plan names no open or upload node, which run engine code only: the executing engine compares it with its graph without them, an edge to an upload moved to its publication job, so one submitted plan validates either path.
